direction.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: single visual-direction reference sheet, landscape exactly 1536x1024 pixels.
Primary request: a faithful 2004 Game Boy Advance Pokemon Emerald visual UI study, with small separate component motifs arranged on one sheet: cream text boxes with navy double pixel frames, restrained teal/green party selection tiles with tiny creature icons and level/HP bars, compact bag pocket tabs with a little backpack icon and item list, and the bottom four-choice FIGHT/BAG/POKEMON/RUN combat command panel. The visual language must be actual early GBA monster RPG, not modern Pokemon menus and not a cozy farming game.
Style/medium: crisp limited-palette raster pixel art with visible hard square 1–2 source-pixel edges, source grammar 240x160 with integer enlargement. Small dark compact glyphs. Navy outlines, pale cream interiors, muted emerald teal.
Composition: one cohesive component direction board on pale green field, with generous separation between primitive specimens, no browser chrome, no glossy cards. A few original green gecko, orange fire bird and blue amphibian motifs. Do not use official logos or claim a real screenshot.
Text: short clear labels HP, Lv12, PARTY, ITEMS, FIGHT, BAG, RUN, 24/36.
Constraints: flat pixel fills, double dark frames, no rounded modern controls, no gradients, no fake scanlines, no watermarks, no decorative wood, no soft antialiasing. This is a generated interpretation for a reference Skill, not an official game screenshot.
direction.inspection: Useful double frames, compact glyphs and command motifs. Soft shading and symmetrical party grid are interpretation errors; written rules override. No official screenshot.

attempts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: reusable transparent pixel sprite atlas, exactly 1536x1024 pixels.
Primary request: a THREE-column TWO-row atlas with exactly SIX separate sprites, each in its equal 512x512 cell. Each sprite centered in its own cell, maximum 340x340 bounding box, at least 15 percent blank gutter on all four cell edges. Row 1 cell 1: original little green leaf gecko monster front view, long curled tail and leaf crest, cheerful. Row 1 cell 2: original little orange fire bird monster front view, tiny wings, yellow beak, red crest, two feet. Row 1 cell 3: original little blue amphibian monster front view, broad head with fin crest, small orange cheek fins, four squat limbs. Row 2 cell 1: purple potion bottle item with white spray top. Row 2 cell 2: red and white capture sphere with dark middle band and small central button. Row 2 cell 3: single red berry with two green leaves.
Style: Game Boy Advance 16-bit monster RPG sprite art, original creatures, very limited color palette, clean square pixel clusters, hard stepped navy outlines, flat 2 or 3 tone shading, no smooth curves or antialiased illustration. Every sprite stands alone, no letters or text.
Background: genuinely transparent RGBA everywhere outside sprites, also transparent gutters. No floor, no shadows under sprites, no background shape, no cell borders, no grid, no checkerboard. No extra objects, no watermark. Six sprites exactly, one per cell.
